correctness.rationale: CRT identifies the quotient by squares with F_2^r and each prime-base image with one Legendre-bit column. Character independence modulo M_t follows from quadratic reciprocity and CRT. Chebyshev prime bounds imply log M_t=O_C(log log X); Siegel-Walfisz makes the r-row Legendre law o(1)-close in total variation to independent uniform rows, including conditioning on distinct sampled primes. Exact full-rank row counting and its infinite-product limit give every asserted distributional formula. The expectation computed is that of the limiting matrix law, not an unproved arithmetic expectation. Verification code passed 130 deterministic finite/exact checks.

value.rationale: The quadratic quotient is a canonical and necessary obstruction to least generation of a unit group. The result supplies an exact natural invariant and its full asymptotic fluctuation law in a growing-prime-factor regime; it quantifies the sharp 0.288788... full-rank fraction at the minimum r prime bases and provides a benchmark for analyzing higher-order character obstructions. This is a meaningful arithmetic synthesis beyond a routine fixed-matrix count.
